title: Shortwave handoff log — dawn->day (scratch)
content:
Shift overview:
- Window: 06:00–14:00 local. Handing off to morning/day squad at 14:00. Quick notes to save you time.
- Tone: mostly stable, one recurring cache-related 503 pattern that needs follow-up (see incident notes).

Incidents and alerts (summary):
1) Cache eviction cascade -> 503s (major, flapping during early hours)
   - First alert: 2026-03-11 02:14 UTC (PagerDuty SEV2)
   - Symptom: token generation requests to hosted API returned 503s with message "KV cache miss overflow" in runtime logs.
   - Temporary mitigation applied: increased cache-memory-limit on serving-runtime pool (node-pool-s1) by +8GB, applied soft-throttle on low-priority routes to drain backlog.
   - Current status: mitigated (soft throttle in place). Root cause unknown — likely a pathological prefix distribution causing KV cache churn.
   - Follow-up tickets: JIRA SRE-4021 (see linked_artifacts) assigned to Priya.

2) Latency spike (minor) 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC
   - 95p latency rose from 120ms -> 1.2s for ~12 minutes.
   - Traced to burst of large-context requests from a single API key; rate-limited and key owner notified.

Quick triage rubric (two-minute read):
- Is API returning 5xx or user-level errors (4xx)? 5xx -> check serving-runtime and load balancer (LB) logs. 4xx -> likely user / prompt issue.
- Check Prometheus dashboards first: total_errors, 5xx_rate, kv_cache_evictions, cluster_cpu_util.
- If kv_cache_evictions > 100/s and 5xx_rate rising -> consider immediate cache limit bump and soft throttle on non-critical routes.

Useful commands (copy/paste):
- Check pod logs (serving runtime): kubectl -n inference logs -l app=serving-runtime -c runtime --since=15m | grep "KV cache miss"
- Increase cache memory (temporary w/ k8s patch): kubectl -n inference patch statefulset serving-runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"CACHE_MEMORY_MB","value":"8192"}] }]}}}}'
- Soft-throttle (feature flag route): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://console.internal/api/route/throttle -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","qps":"20"}'
- Quick health check (prometheus): curl -g 'http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_evictions%5B5m%5D' | jq

Escalation & contacts:
- Primary SRE oncall: Priya Singh (Slack @priya, mobile +1-555-0142)
- Runtime lead: Marco Alvarez (Slack @marco, mobile +1-555-0199)
- Product ops (for customer-impacting throttles): ops@redwood.com
- If infra nodes OOM/eviction across pool -> escalate to infra team (channel #infra-core).

Temporary procedures enacted (what I did):
- Increased CACHE_MEMORY_MB on node-pool-s1 statefulset (see command above).
- Added soft throttle to /v1/generate at qps=20 for the lowest-tier keys to reduce churn.
- Deployed a lightweight sampling logger to collect 1% of failing requests with full headers for offline analysis (PR: redwood/runtime#1283).

Data to hand off for deep-dive:
- Prometheus queries collected: kv_cache_evictions (last 24h), runtime_5xx_rate (30m windows), per-client request sizes distribution. Stored snapshot: s3://redwood-debug/shortwave/2026-03-11-metrics-snapshot.json
- Saved log slice from runtime pods: /tmp/shortwave-runtime-logs-2026-03-11.tgz (pushed to artifact store)

Notes-to-self (rough):
- The eviction pattern correlates with a new user sending very long prefix sequences around 01:45 UTC. Need to correlate with customer API key (we flagged and notified owner).
- Check whether new kernel selection changes in last runtime build could have affected KV retention (PRs in last 72h). Marco to cross-check.

Open questions / follow-ups (assign or track):
- Q1: Is cache eviction policy too eager for small-model variants? (Ticket: SRE-4021)
- Q2: Should we implement per-key prefix-length caps at the gateway? quick wins vs product tradeoffs. (Discuss with product-hosted-api)
- Q3: Is the soft-throttle logic wired into cost-accounting? need billing team input.

To-do before next shift (concrete):
- Priya: collect heap profiles from node-pool-s1 for last 36h (attach to ticket).
- Marco: review runtime kernel selection commits between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-11.
- Me (Evan): prepare a small DB of offending API keys + request samples and push to /sre/handovers (permission: s3://redwood-sre/handovers).

Quick checklist for morning/next oncall:
[ ] Verify soft-throttle is still active and not over-throttling customer traffic.
[ ] Confirm cache-memory bump persisted after rollout (some automated rollback jobs may revert changes).
[ ] Validate that sampled failing requests are present in artifact store and accessible.
[ ] Check if any new alerts for kv_cache_evictions or runtime_ooms fired after 06:00.

Other small notes / scratch bits: 
- Idea: add a "cold-prefix" detector that tags keys with pathological prefix distribution and automatically routes them to a low-memory footprint runtime variant for a probation window. POC idea — low priority.
- Misc commands: redis-cli -h redis-rt info memory | grep used_memory_human

End of handoff. Ping me on Slack if anything gone dark before the morning handoff — I’ll be awake for the next hour (~until 15:00 local).

-- Evan
